children: Johnson & Johnson (NYSE:JNJ) raised 2026 guidance after beating Q1–Q2 results, touted oncology and medtech momentum (DARZALEX, CAR-T, CARVYKTI, VARIPULSE) plus pipeline wins like PAPILLON and a Firefly buyout, proposed a $5.5B talc deal and expects steady growth and dividends.
Previous Week Recap
JNJ Revenue Guidance Raised
: Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) beat Q1–Q2 2026 revenue and EPS, raised 2026 guidance to ~6.5% organic sales growth and ~7.3% adjusted EPS growth, and expects 2026 revenue above $100B.
PAPILLON Phase 3; OS, PFS2 Gains
: JNJ: Phase 3 PAPILLON — IV RYBREVANT + chemo vs chemo in EGFR exon 20 ins NSCLC: median OS 34.3 vs 27.9 months; PFS2 28.3 vs 17.5 months; 43% death-risk reduction (adjusted).
Double-Digit Enterprise Growth Outlook
: JNJ expects double-digit enterprise growth in coming years, citing pharma pipeline, medtech strength and capital flexibility. 2026 loss-of-exclusivity exposure estimated at about $4.0–$4.5B.
Talc Settlement Proposed; No Uncertainty

: Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) proposed a $5.5 billion talc settlement, said to be below a prior figure. Management expects no further financial uncertainty and plans to keep investing and paying dividends.
oncology Target And Assets

: Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) targets $50B oncology sales (ex-acquisitions) and highlights oncology assets DARZALEX, CAR-T, TALVEY, ramantamig; immunology assets icotrokinra, IMAAVY, pasrodimab, JNJ-4804.
MOONLIGHT-1 Endpoints Missed

: Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) said Phase 2 MOONLIGHT-1 trial of JNJ-5120 missed its primary efficacy endpoint (MADRS Day 5 vs placebo). Drug was generally well tolerated; company is reviewing full dataset.
Firefly Bio Buyout Completed
: JNJ closed a $1B July buyout of Firefly Bio, adding a preclinical pan‑KRAS candidate targeting pancreatic, colorectal and lung cancers to its early‑stage oncology pipeline.
Caplyta Data: Sexual Function
: JNJ reported late-stage data: adding 42 mg Caplyta to antidepressants improved sexual function in 480 MDD patients with prior inadequate response; no benefit for those without baseline dysfunction.
CARVYKTI Commercialization Partnership
: Johnson & Johnson partners to commercialize CARVYKTI (ciltacabtagene autoleucel). CARVYKTI sold in 19 markets via 348 centers; Legend reported Q2 sales ~$657M, H1 2026 ~$1.25B, 2025 est ~$1.9B.
VARIPULSE Installed, Europe Launch
: Johnson & Johnson (JNJ): VARIPULSE treated 100,000+ patients; ~6,300 CARTO mapping systems installed; VARIPULSE Pro launched in Europe, U.S. launch expected soon.
